107	### Core Rules
108	
109	*Every rule below is a sim rule of the Emitter State owner module (`src/sim/emitter/`), stated so that an implementer can write it and a tester can falsify it. Registry constants are cited by their registered name (`TICK_RATE` 60, `TILE_PX` 48, `AIM_UNITS` 4096, `REACH_PX` 72, `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, `rng_derive`, `state_hash`, `hook_runs_this_tick`, `chest_point`, `power_allocation`, `served_pm`, and the Graph's `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 / `INRUSH_PM` 1500) and are never restated with another value; owner-GDD tuning rows that are not registry entries (the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD`, `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS`, `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`) are cited by name the same way. Every number this GDD introduces has its own name and the tag "placeholder, owner X, confirmed by Y" (Tuning Knobs); a number another GDD owns is cited by that GDD's name for it. Where a rule records an alternative that was considered and rejected, the rejection is part of the rule: a later change must answer it. Markers: "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" records a point where the specialists disagreed and the rulings, or a pick, decided; "(provisional — X …)" marks an assumption about a counterpart's text that is not yet confirmed; as of 2026-10-27 every counterpart GDD is Status Designed, so a provisional tag now waits on a named counterpart sentence, not on a missing GDD. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)**
110	
111	**EM-1 — One block, one hook, one truth.** Emitter State is exactly one persisted `SIM` state block, `emitter.state` (owner Emitter State; `class` SIM; `persist` true; `persist_scope` WORLD; `scope` SHARED; `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY; `schema_version` 1; **`supported_versions` [1]; `added_in_format` 1** (Save/Load SL-15 items 2 and 7: the boot lints `SL_BOOT_NO_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` and `SL_BOOT_NO_ADDED_IN_FORMAT` refuse a persisted block that declares no `supported_versions` containing its own current `schema_version`, or has no `added_in_format` entry in the format data file; because MVP death means restart from the last autosave, restore is the main recovery path and a block that cannot boot or pre-check would strand it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` (`layout.state` is Layout's registered block and `body.state` is Ship Body's BDY-5 block, both designed; the Graph's `restore_after: [layout.state]` and the Controller's PC-14 are the precedents) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* — fixture anchors and occluding rectangles need the Layout, lamp nodes need the Graph, the beam's foot origin and frame need Body, and the chest point and aim need the Controller; the three-block list in the context brief omitted `body.state` and is superseded), registered by the module's composition-root call during BOOTING (kernel CR-6, CR-8). Exactly one step hook, `emitter.place` (divisor 1, offset 0, `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`), does all per-tick work: beam pose, output, lifecycle, the subject table. Its position after `body.integrate` is fixed by PC-15 and the registry comment on `hook_runs_this_tick` ("Controller/Body/Emitter 1"); the second entry, `graph.propagate.failure`, is this GDD's (the wording refresh owed to PC-15 is in Cross-References); no second Emitter hook exists in the MVP, because placement, lamp reads, fault glow and the subject table all need the same ordered reads. Hook ids are written exactly: `graph.propagate.power`, `graph.propagate.atmo`, `suit.vitals`, `controller.step`, `body.integrate`, `emitter.place`; the kernel has no alias concept and an unknown id or a cycle fails boot (CR-3), so the three Graph hook ids are always written with their phase suffix. The direct entry `after: graph.propagate.failure` puts `emitter.place`, on every Graph tick, after all three Graph hooks (`graph.propagate.power` → `graph.propagate.atmo` → `graph.propagate.failure`, Graph LS-8), so the hook reads the state the Graph run just produced — served power, node state after the failure phase and the descriptor list — and a snapshot taken at that tick and restored gives `validate` at the next tick the same subject table (kernel G4). **Terminology: "Graph tick"** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: under the Graph's baseline stagger (LS-8: power offset 0, atmo 2, failure 4) "Graph tick" in this GDD means two different ticks. (a) For input timing (`arm_tick` rounding, M14 consumed by phase 0, assumption A1, the D.2 examples `T_a` 1200, 126 and 132) it is the power-hook tick, `T mod 6 = 0`. (b) For reads (the descriptor list, node `state`, the fault-glow reconciliation, AC-43b / AC-61 / AC-62 "on the Graph tick of its descriptor") it is the failure-hook tick, `T mod 6 = 4`, on which `emitter.place` runs after `graph.propagate.failure` and sees that step's final state; `served_pm` (phase 2) changes on `T mod 6 = 0`. A glow therefore appears on the failure tick of the step in which its descriptor appears, never later. No numeric value or hook registration changes (`emitter.place` stays (1, 0) after `[body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`). The second chain, `graph.propagate.atmo` → `suit.vitals` (divisor 6) → `controller.step` → `body.integrate` → `emitter.place`, fixes where Suit's `force_off` lands (EM-10): `suit.vitals` is `after: graph.propagate.atmo` (Graph LS-8) and `controller.step` is `after: suit.vitals` (PC-15). That chain is **assumption A2, locked by PC-15 and LS-8; Suit must keep the id** `suit.vitals` (Suit & Equipment, designed, keeps it with `after: graph.propagate.atmo`: SE-8); the lamp latency of D.2 no longer depends on it. In `MIRROR` mode the hook never runs; the replica reads the replicated `SHARED_SUMMARY`, which in VS-B must carry the beam's origin, aim, shape and switch (derived values the host publishes) so a remote client can draw a crewmate's beam (an ask to Save/Load and Co-op). The module is scene-tree free, headless-testable and deterministic (same seed and command stream → identical `state_hash`).
112	
113	**EM-2 — Vocabulary: the two `lit`s, kept verbatim.** The Controller locks `emitter.state.lit` as a *record field* (PC acceptance criteria test it on the seat's beam) and `lit(o)` as the *exposure query* (PC-6, PC D.9). Both names stay exactly as the Controller wrote them; renaming either breaks the Controller's tests. (a) **`emitter.state.lit`** — the record field: true iff the emitter's `output_pm > 0` (any kind). It means "this emitter is emitting". Suit's `suit.vitals` reads it on the seat's beam to drain charge; the Presenter draws a beam only when it is true. (b) **`lit(subject)`** — the query: the hysteresis-filtered comparison of a subject's action-gating light, `act_lux_pm`, against the threshold `LIT_ON_PM` / `LIT_OFF_PM` (EM-22). It means "this thing is lit enough to read and touch". Related terms: **`output_pm`** — an emitter's own steady brightness, integer 0..1000 permille; **`reach_px`** — an emitter's current outer radius in base px; **`lux_pm`** — a subject's total light, the saturating sum of every contribution at its anchor, integer 0..1000, read by Horror Entities (Attention reads the `emitters()` list, never `lux_pm`; Attention AT-4); **`act_lux_pm`** — the same sum restricted to emitters that gate actions (the BEACON does not); **`top_emitter_id`** — the emitter with the largest contribution to a subject (ties by ascending id). These two `lit`s are also defined in the Summary glossary line.
114	
115	**EM-3 — Six emitter kinds, a closed list.** An emitter is one of BEAM, FIXTURE (two subkinds mark the **self-powered fixture class**, `node_ref` 0: EMERGENCY, the declared cryo-bay lamp, authored by Derelict Authoring DA-23 as `fixture_subkind_emergency`; and DOCK_STATUS, the small status glow on the docked pod's dock-room prop, one per dock room, authored by Derelict Authoring as `fixture_subkind_dock_status` *(name proposed here, for Derelict Authoring and Web Map to confirm)* — an ordinary lit fixture, not a further `act_gate` exception *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, which makes the pod console's lit gate always satisfied; every other fixture carries no subkind and is a Graph LOAD) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*, NODE_LANTERN, DEPLOYABLE (subkind GLOWSTICK in the MVP; FLARE, TORCH, DECOY in VS-A), BEACON or FAULT_GLOW. A seventh kind is a schema bump (registry: `emitter_kind`). No record carries a `phantom`, `perceived`, `decoy` or `hallucinated` field of any kind (EM-29).
116	
117	| Kind | Created by / when | Removed by | Switch | Power | Layer | `gates_actions` | Id |

### Core Rules

*Every rule below is a sim rule of the Emitter State owner module (`src/sim/emitter/`), stated so that an implementer can write it and a tester can falsify it. Registry constants are cited by their registered name (`TICK_RATE` 60, `TILE_PX` 48, `AIM_UNITS` 4096, `REACH_PX` 72, `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, `rng_derive`, `state_hash`, `hook_runs_this_tick`, `chest_point`, `power_allocation`, `served_pm`, and the Graph's `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 / `INRUSH_PM` 1500) and are never restated with another value; owner-GDD tuning rows that are not registry entries (the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD`, `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS`, `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`) are cited by name the same way. Every number this GDD introduces has its own name and the tag "placeholder, owner X, confirmed by Y" (Tuning Knobs); a number another GDD owns is cited by that GDD's name for it. Where a rule records an alternative that was considered and rejected, the rejection is part of the rule: a later change must answer it. Markers: "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" records a point where the specialists disagreed and the rulings, or a pick, decided; "(provisional — X …)" marks an assumption about a counterpart's text that is not yet confirmed; as of 2026-10-27 every counterpart GDD is Status Designed, so a provisional tag now waits on a named counterpart sentence, not on a missing GDD. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)**

**EM-1 — One block, one hook, one truth.** Emitter State is exactly one persisted `SIM` state block, `emitter.state` (owner Emitter State; `class` SIM; `persist` true; `persist_scope` WORLD; `scope` SHARED; `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY; `schema_version` 1; **`supported_versions` [1]; `added_in_format` 1** (Save/Load SL-15 items 2 and 7: the boot lints `SL_BOOT_NO_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` and `SL_BOOT_NO_ADDED_IN_FORMAT` refuse a persisted block that declares no `supported_versions` containing its own current `schema_version`, or has no `added_in_format` entry in the format data file; because MVP death means restart from the last autosave, restore is the main recovery path and a block that cannot boot or pre-check would strand it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` (`layout.state` is Layout's registered block and `body.state` is Ship Body's BDY-5 block, both designed; the Graph's `restore_after: [layout.state]` and the Controller's PC-14 are the precedents) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* — fixture anchors and occluding rectangles need the Layout, lamp nodes need the Graph, the beam's foot origin and frame need Body, and the chest point and aim need the Controller; the three-block list in the context brief omitted `body.state` and is superseded), registered by the module's composition-root call during BOOTING (kernel CR-6, CR-8). Exactly one step hook, `emitter.place` (divisor 1, offset 0, `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`), does all per-tick work: beam pose, output, lifecycle, the subject table. Its position after `body.integrate` is fixed by PC-15 and the registry comment on `hook_runs_this_tick` ("Controller/Body/Emitter 1"); the second entry, `graph.propagate.failure`, is this GDD's (the wording refresh owed to PC-15 is in Cross-References); no second Emitter hook exists in the MVP, because placement, lamp reads, fault glow and the subject table all need the same ordered reads. Hook ids are written exactly: `graph.propagate.power`, `graph.propagate.atmo`, `suit.vitals`, `controller.step`, `body.integrate`, `emitter.place`; the kernel has no alias concept and an unknown id or a cycle fails boot (CR-3), so the three Graph hook ids are always written with their phase suffix. The direct entry `after: graph.propagate.failure` puts `emitter.place`, on every Graph tick, after all three Graph hooks (`graph.propagate.power` → `graph.propagate.atmo` → `graph.propagate.failure`, Graph LS-8), so the hook reads the state the Graph run just produced — served power, node state after the failure phase and the descriptor list — and a snapshot taken at that tick and restored gives `validate` at the next tick the same subject table (kernel G4). **Terminology: "Graph tick"** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: under the Graph's baseline stagger (LS-8: power offset 0, atmo 2, failure 4) "Graph tick" in this GDD means two different ticks. (a) For input timing (`arm_tick` rounding, M14 consumed by phase 0, assumption A1, the D.2 examples `T_a` 1200, 126 and 132) it is the power-hook tick, `T mod 6 = 0`. (b) For reads (the descriptor list, node `state`, the fault-glow reconciliation, AC-43b / AC-61 / AC-62 "on the Graph tick of its descriptor") it is the failure-hook tick, `T mod 6 = 4`, on which `emitter.place` runs after `graph.propagate.failure` and sees that step's final state; `served_pm` (phase 2) changes on `T mod 6 = 0`. A glow therefore appears on the failure tick of the step in which its descriptor appears, never later. No numeric value or hook registration changes (`emitter.place` stays (1, 0) after `[body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`). The second chain, `graph.propagate.atmo` → `suit.vitals` (divisor 6) → `controller.step` → `body.integrate` → `emitter.place`, fixes where Suit's `force_off` lands (EM-10): `suit.vitals` is `after: graph.propagate.atmo` (Graph LS-8) and `controller.step` is `after: suit.vitals` (PC-15). That chain is **assumption A2, locked by PC-15 and LS-8; Suit must keep the id** `suit.vitals` (Suit & Equipment, designed, keeps it with `after: graph.propagate.atmo`: SE-8); the lamp latency of D.2 no longer depends on it. In `MIRROR` mode the hook never runs; the replica reads the replicated `SHARED_SUMMARY`, which in VS-B must carry the beam's origin, aim, shape and switch (derived values the host publishes) so a remote client can draw a crewmate's beam (an ask to Save/Load and Co-op). The module is scene-tree free, headless-testable and deterministic (same seed and command stream → identical `state_hash`).

**EM-2 — Vocabulary: the two `lit`s, kept verbatim.** The Controller locks `emitter.state.lit` as a *record field* (PC acceptance criteria test it on the seat's beam) and `lit(o)` as the *exposure query* (PC-6, PC D.9). Both names stay exactly as the Controller wrote them; renaming either breaks the Controller's tests. (a) **`emitter.state.lit`** — the record field: true iff the emitter's `output_pm > 0` (any kind). It means "this emitter is emitting". Suit's `suit.vitals` reads it on the seat's beam to drain charge; the Presenter draws a beam only when it is true. (b) **`lit(subject)`** — the query: the hysteresis-filtered comparison of a subject's action-gating light, `act_lux_pm`, against the threshold `LIT_ON_PM` / `LIT_OFF_PM` (EM-22). It means "this thing is lit enough to read and touch". Related terms: **`output_pm`** — an emitter's own steady brightness, integer 0..1000 permille; **`reach_px`** — an emitter's current outer radius in base px; **`lux_pm`** — a subject's total light, the saturating sum of every contribution at its anchor, integer 0..1000, read by Horror Entities (Attention reads the `emitters()` list, never `lux_pm`; Attention AT-4); **`act_lux_pm`** — the same sum restricted to emitters that gate actions (the BEACON does not); **`top_emitter_id`** — the emitter with the largest contribution to a subject (ties by ascending id). These two `lit`s are also defined in the Summary glossary line.

**EM-3 — Six emitter kinds, a closed list.** An emitter is one of BEAM, FIXTURE (two subkinds mark the **self-powered fixture class**, `node_ref` 0: EMERGENCY, the declared cryo-bay lamp, authored by Derelict Authoring DA-23 as `fixture_subkind_emergency`; and DOCK_STATUS, the small status glow on the docked pod's dock-room prop, one per dock room, authored by Derelict Authoring as `fixture_subkind_dock_status` *(name proposed here, for Derelict Authoring and Web Map to confirm)* — an ordinary lit fixture, not a further `act_gate` exception *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, which makes the pod console's lit gate always satisfied; every other fixture carries no subkind and is a Graph LOAD) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*, NODE_LANTERN, DEPLOYABLE (subkind GLOWSTICK in the MVP; FLARE, TORCH, DECOY in VS-A), BEACON or FAULT_GLOW. A seventh kind is a schema bump (registry: `emitter_kind`). No record carries a `phantom`, `perceived`, `decoy` or `hallucinated` field of any kind (EM-29).

Both are **reads** of `controller.state` inside `emitter.place`, never commands: aim is not an Emitter command (the kernel row's "set/toggle/aim commands" wording is refreshed in Cross-References). The tool-grip anchor `HAND_POINT` is lightless and is never read by this block, and no rule anywhere names it an origin. The beam follows *aim*, not facing: facing diverges from aim while running (PC-4 rule 3). The drawn cone and the simulated cone may diverge by up to the PC-5 accepted tolerance (≤ 2.8°, ≤ 1 tick; the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` / `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` knobs widen it to 3 ticks), which is why the agreement test (design test 1) is stated at rest. **Occlusion starts at the foot, not the chest** *(orchestrator ruling: the foot-origin rule of the technical-director over the systems-designer's sanitised walk-back, because `pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction — `LocomotionStep` keeps the avatar's box out of them — and is free of the 2 px mirror jitter; the walk-back remains the documented alternative, ADR candidate 5)*: `CHEST_POINT.y` is -45..-25 px (`h` = −y, 25..45), so with a 24 px wall footprint the chest point stands *inside* the footprint whenever the feet are `s` px south of the first legal row in front of a north wall (`s` = 0 on that row, LY-8 b) with `h − 24 ≤ s ≤ h − 1`: the band is **1–44 px** over all animation rows (10–33 px for the walk row at `h` 34 — the first draft's "10-34" was one row's band, not the range). Other emitter kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What ships for each Lighting-spike outcome** (2D Lighting LO-10; its spike step 3b is a **pre-implementation gate for ADR candidate 5**, not a later check): outcome **B** (the light's `offset` moves the apex without moving the shadow origin) — the foot-origin rule ships as written and Lighting draws the shadow from the foot; outcome **A** (the shadow originates at the chest) with AC-57 passing — the foot-origin rule ships and the residual discrepancy (≤ 2 base px) is recorded; outcome A with AC-57 failing (a beam that renders black, or leaks through the wall, while the sim reports the opposite) — outcome **D** ships: ADR 5 adopts the walk-back (the sim occludes from the chest, walked back to the first clear point on the segment to the foot), D.4, EM-20 g and AC-10 are re-derived, and nothing else in this GDD changes. The shape table below is **data owned by this GDD as the carrier of the art bible 8.3 rows** (registry: `light_shape`) so that the queried edge and the drawn edge cannot drift: Lighting's textures and cone geometry derive from it, with a build lint that the rendered reach equals the table reach ±1 px for hard-edged rows (EM-26). The split beam's blind spot is its identity: two cones with a dark wedge that never closes — the one shape that can never see straight ahead. 210	**EM-9 — The beam in every actionable state; DOWNED keeps it, DEAD ends it.** The beam is available while the actor is IDLE, WALK, RUN, CARRY_WALK or CHANNELLING (PC-8; the user's chest-lamp decision: nothing the hands do touches the lamp). While `loco_state == DOWNED` the beam keeps its committed state — the aim is frozen at the last committed value and the origin is the `chest_sim` of the down animation row; a downed crewmate is a locator (P1) — which is the handoff PC left to this GDD ("Emitter State decides what a downed emitter does"). While STAGGERED the state is likewise unchanged. At the tick `emitter.place` reads `loco_state == DEAD`, it forces `switch_on` false (the Controller's `DEAD` row: "beam off (Emitter State on actor death)") as an `emitter.place`-internal `force_off`, a read of `controller.state` with no command. Because Save/Load's death stub restarts from the last autosave through `request_restore` at that tick's P6, the DEAD-tick off-state is unobservable in the MVP (say so in tests). A beam that stays on over a corpse until Suit's charge runs out — a corpse as a lantern the web can see — is *not* a rule here; it is a VS-B question for Attention and Sanity (Open Questions). In IN_POD the beam follows its actor into the pod's body frame (EM-30; Ship Body's `body_of_actor` carries the frame and Web Map & Transit is designed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
211	
212	**EM-10 — Beam charge is Suit's.** Suit & Equipment owns charge, drain, `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the HUD "beam and tool charge" reading (art bible HUD set). `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's charge view and rejects a turn-ON at zero charge with `CHARGE_EMPTY`; a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge (the strobe floor `TOO_SOON` of EM-7 applies to both directions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Suit's divisor-6 `suit.vitals` reads `emitter.state.lit` on the seat's beam to drain charge and calls `force_off(beam_id)` (E5) at zero; because `suit.vitals` runs earlier in the tick than `emitter.place`, a `force_off` takes effect in the same tick's `emitter.place`, and the owner's six-tick re-check (EM-25) then finds a channelled target unlit and aborts, so at most five ticks of channel run on a dark target. The beam is a *suit load, not a ship LOAD*: Emitter State never calls `set_load_request` for it and the Graph is not involved. (Suit & Equipment, designed: SE-8; Suit keeps the hook name `suit.vitals` and its `after: graph.propagate.atmo`.)
213	
214	**EM-11 — Fixtures are switchable Graph LOADs; the lamp formula gates on the switch.** A FIXTURE carries `node_ref` (a Graph `13 LOAD` node of the LOAD subtype `LAMP` — the Item DB assigns the subtype id, currently `2 LAMP`; the Graph names only `HEATER`; provisional), `base_pm` (from the def's `emits`) and `switch_on`. Its brightness is `lamp_output_pm` (Formulas D.1): `output_pm = switch_on and armed and live ? ⌊base_pm * served_pm / 1000⌋ : 0`. The lit branch is the registry formula `power_allocation`'s output "lamp brightness = base * served_pm / 1000", reused verbatim. **`served_pm` is the tier's satisfaction `sat_k`, independent of the node's own request** (Graph D.6), so a switched-off lamp can still read `served_pm` 1000: the Emitter's own `switch_on` is the gate, not the Graph, or an off lamp would shine. Power draw is a Graph LOAD: inside the `set_switch` apply the Emitter calls M14 `set_load_request(node_ref, req_w)` with `req_w` the def's rated draw (Graph MVP: 20 W) when on and 0 when off (Class B: it clamps to `0..req_max`, queues to the next Graph phase 0, and is a no-op on an unknown, tombstoned, dormant or SALVAGED node). A lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (Graph P1); under re-energise inrush the bank draws `req_w * INRUSH_PM / 1000` for `INRUSH_STEPS` runs, which can dim the tier-3 bank for half a second — the Graph's business, visible as an honest dip, changing no Emitter rule. The Emitter never recomputes watts and never calls M14 for node lanterns or the beam. A FIXTURE with `node_ref` 0 is *self-powered*: permitted only for the two declared subkinds, EMERGENCY (the cryo-bay emergency lamp, exactly one in the world, declared by Derelict Authoring DA-23 as `fixture_subkind_emergency`) and DOCK_STATUS (below); it has no M14 call, no ARMING and a fixed `base_pm`, and any other `node_ref` 0 fixture is refused by the authoring lint and at boot (`SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`: exactly one EMERGENCY, exactly one DOCK_STATUS per dock room, none elsewhere). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; second subkind added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)* **The DOCK_STATUS fixture (user ruling X2, 2026-10-27)** keeps the pod console's lit gate satisfied at every dock without a further `act_gate` exception *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (Interaction's IA-6 refusal of a `pod_hop` exemption stands): it is an *ordinary lit fixture* (`gates_actions` true, SOFT curve, counted in `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `section_emission`, so the web can read it like any lamp, P3 and "light is never free"), authored by Derelict Authoring on the dock room's docked-podcraft prop, in the **dock room's section** and not on the pod body (the pod section is dormant always, Web Map WM-5, and the lamp must not depend on it). It is created and discarded with its section (E1, E2), has no `node_ref` and therefore no liveness test (EM-13 concerns Graph nodes) and cannot be failed, starved or drained by any ship state, which is the point: the stranded player always finds the console lit. Its `switch_on` is driven only by the mutator **E10 `set_dock_status(section_id, on)`**, which Web Map & Transit calls in the apply that writes `pod_at` (on for the dock room the pod parks at, off for the one it leaves; the berth and unberth verbs are the derelict weld verbs and have nothing to do with it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the first draft named the berth and unberth applies, and read `pod_at` at E1)*, so the glow emits only while the pod is there. **E1 creates every DOCK_STATUS glow switched off and reads nothing of Web Map's state**: E1 runs at `init_world` step 2, before Web Map writes `pod_at` at step 7, so the home dock's glow is switched on by Web Map's step-7 call to E10 (`pod_at` HOME) in the same `init_world` apply, and the derelict docks' glows stay off until the pod parks there. `set_switch` of either origin is refused `NOT_SWITCHABLE` for this subkind and Interaction registers no switch interactable for it; it takes no M14 call and no ARMING, and E10 has no commit-spacing guard and writes no `last_toggle_tick` (E10's row in EM-5 gives the reason: the pod's own timing spaces the transitions, and an atomic apply could not observe a refusal) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Values** (placeholders, owner game-designer and art-director, confirmed by the Lighting spike; derivation in D.1b): `DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` 500, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX` 48, shape row 7 (`FIXTURE`, SOFT) at that reach, and the placement constraint `DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX` 24 (the console subject's anchor lies within 24 px of the glow origin, clear of every occluder). Its luminance and hue sit outside the visible-unknown lamp's band (the art-director's, not this GDD's; a Lighting `hue_class` token owed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
215	
216	**EM-12 — One latency story for switching.** A `set_switch` applies at P2 of tick `T_a`; its M14 call is queued to the next Graph phase 0; the lamp is **ARMING with `output_pm` 0** until `arm_tick`, the first `graph.propagate.power` run that consumed the request, and is lit on the first `emitter.place` at or after it (Formulas D.2 `switch_latency`: `arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`). Under the stated assumptions the lamp is lit between 0 and `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks after the apply — at most 83 ms — and no single number from this paragraph is a design fact: D.2 derives the range with a worked example at both alignments (switch on a Graph tick; switch on the tick after one). **Assumption A1 (derived, not assumed; confirmed by the Graph 2026-10-27 in its Interactions row for this system):** kernel CR-2 ("P3 sees all of P2") and Graph LS-8 phase 0 ("apply queued unconditional inputs: `set_load_request` changes") together mean that an M14 call made in P2 of a Graph tick is consumed by that same tick's phase 0, so the range is 0..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks; the negative case, a Graph that applied only strictly later requests, would give 1..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` and is kept in D.2 as the labelled alternative. The direct `after: graph.propagate.failure` entry (EM-1) guarantees that the hook reads that run's output on the same tick. Switching **off** is immediate (`output_pm` 0 from the apply tick; M14 `(node_ref, 0)`); an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels the pending ON and is not a realised transition (it writes no `last_toggle_tick`, EM-7, D.2b). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32)* The same "light changes only on committed state" rule PC-5 states for the beam holds for fixtures; the asymmetry (ON waits for the Graph pulse, OFF does not) is deliberate and physical: the ship has to serve the lamp, and the lamp cannot go on ahead of the ship. Fixtures never pre-play light; the wall-switch click and animation pre-play. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**EM-6 — The beam is a chest emitter.** For the seat's BEAM the *apex* and the *reach* are measured from `controller.state.chest_sim` (= `pos_curr + CHEST_POINT[sheet][anim] (.) mirror`, `|x| <= 2` px, registry `chest_point`; PC D.12), and the *axis* is the committed `aim_angle` (1/4096 turn, `AIM_UNITS` 4096; 0 = E, counter-clockwise, spawn aim 3072 = S). Both are **reads** of `controller.state` inside `emitter.place`, never commands: aim is not an Emitter command (the kernel row's "set/toggle/aim commands" wording is refreshed in Cross-References). The tool-grip anchor `HAND_POINT` is lightless and is never read by this block, and no rule anywhere names it an origin. The beam follows *aim*, not facing: facing diverges from aim while running (PC-4 rule 3). The drawn cone and the simulated cone may diverge by up to the PC-5 accepted tolerance (≤ 2.8°, ≤ 1 tick; the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` / `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` knobs widen it to 3 ticks), which is why the agreement test (design test 1) is stated at rest. **Occlusion starts at the foot, not the chest** *(orchestrator ruling: the foot-origin rule of the technical-director over the systems-designer's sanitised walk-back, because `pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction — `LocomotionStep` keeps the avatar's box out of them — and is free of the 2 px mirror jitter; the walk-back remains the documented alternative, ADR candidate 5)*: `CHEST_POINT.y` is -45..-25 px (`h` = −y, 25..45), so with a 24 px wall footprint the chest point stands *inside* the footprint whenever the feet are `s` px south of the first legal row in front of a north wall (`s` = 0 on that row, LY-8 b) with `h − 24 ≤ s ≤ h − 1`: the band is **1–44 px** over all animation rows (10–33 px for the walk row at `h` 34 — the first draft's "10-34" was one row's band, not the range). Walls east or west of the avatar cost at most the 4 px of chest-x offset. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The cone's apex, reach and distance are therefore measured from the chest, while the occluder segment to a subject starts at the foot origin (`pos_curr`, `beam_pose`). Other emitter kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What ships for each Lighting-spike outcome** (2D Lighting LO-10; its spike step 3b is a **pre-implementation gate for ADR candidate 5**, not a later check): outcome **B** (the light's `offset` moves the apex without moving the shadow origin) — the foot-origin rule ships as written and Lighting draws the shadow from the foot; outcome **A** (the shadow originates at the chest) with AC-57 passing — the foot-origin rule ships and the residual discrepancy (≤ 2 base px) is recorded; outcome A with AC-57 failing (a beam that renders black, or leaks through the wall, while the sim reports the opposite) — outcome **D** ships: ADR 5 adopts the walk-back (the sim occludes from the chest, walked back to the first clear point on the segment to the foot), D.4, EM-20 g and AC-10 are re-derived, and nothing else in this GDD changes. Until the spike reports, the foot-origin rule is the working rule and the worst case — a beam that renders black while the sim reports it lit, which would happen every time a player walks up to a wall — is an open risk (Open Question 5). **Near-field is aim-dependent, and the ruled answer is a drawn foot pool, not a control tax** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; ruled 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D24)*: an object between the lamp and the feet in screen-y is behind the apex when the player faces up-screen; the cone is honest about it (nothing in the drawn cone reaches it either) and the sim adds no hidden compensation. The first draft called this "a skill expression"; the systems-designer, endorsed by the creative-director, reads it as a **control tax caused by the chest-lamp decision**: an object at the player's feet, or one tile to the side, is dark in every shape in any unlit room even though it is inside Interaction's `REACH_PX` 72, and it will read as a broken prompt, not as horror. P1 is preserved if the spill is *drawn*; the price is a small loss of P3 darkness right at the body. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions):** `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` ships at **24 px** (range 0–48; 0 switches the spill off) with `BEAM_SPILL_PM` 600 registered, as a dim, drawn, honest pool that gates actions only within its own actionable radius `r_lit_px` of the feet (18 px at the defaults, D.7 chain) and contributes minimally to exposure; Interaction's `REACH_PX` 72 is a different, larger distance (the hand's reach) and the spill does not light everything inside it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; it is validated by the *dark-at-feet* metric of the first playtest (the playtest stub's placeholder decision line is 5 % of lit-beam ticks; Open Question 17). The user's chest-lamp decision stands unchanged: the lamp is still on the chest and still the only light that follows the player; the spill is a small, honest, drawn pool at the feet. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The mechanics were fixed ahead of the ruling so that the ruling is one data value: the spill is one extra SOFT, omnidirectional, non-shadow contribution of the BEAM record, centred on the foot origin (`occ_origin`), of reach `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` and output `BEAM_SPILL_PM` (600, range 150–1000, owner game-designer; registered), present only while the beam is on (the beam record's `switch_on`, so the spill flips with the beam and adds no transition of its own to the commit-spacing guard), tested with the ordinary radius, occlusion and clearance rules, added to the `act_lux_pm` and `lux_pm` of objects (never to the owner's ACTOR self-lux, EM-21) and **excluded from `section_emission`** (D.12 counts the beam's cone term alone, so the spill adds no Attention load). At 24 px and 600 permille its actionable radius `r_lit_px` is **18 px, read from the D.7 integer chain** (the retired closed form ⌊24 × 450 / 600⌋ agrees at this one point and is not used; at d = 18, f = ⌊1000 × 6 / 24⌋ = 250 and c = ⌊600 × 250 / 1000⌋ = 150 = `LIT_ON_PM`; at d = 19, f = 208 and c = 124 < 150): it covers an object at the feet and not one a full tile (48 px) to the side; **no legal setting reaches a full tile**: at the maximum radius 48 and the maximum output 1000 the chain gives `r_lit_px` 40 (at d = 40, f = 166 and c = 166; at d = 41, f = 145 and c = 145), so "48 px to the side" is dark by design at every value in range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Subject kinds it applies to:** every registered subject kind except the owner's own ACTOR (EM-21 keeps the owner's self-lux at the beam's apex value): OBJECT, ITEM, a second seat's ACTOR (VS-B) and HORROR, each through the ordinary radius, occlusion and clearance rules; a horror within the spill's radius of the player's feet therefore reads lit (`lux_pm` up to 600), which is honest exposure and is not a special case (AC-10c). **The spill is published to Lighting** through the read-view accessor `beam_spill(beam_id)` (EM-26), not through `emitters()`, so that the sim edge and the drawn edge can be proved equal and so that Attention's list never counts it. It is `light_shape` row 11 `BEAM_SPILL` (a registry entry this GDD owns; see EM-8): a **conditional** row, present in the shape table iff `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0, and it needs a Lighting texture and AC-10b. A non-zero radius must also satisfy I-REACH (at least `REACH_MIN_PX` 24), so the effective range is 0 (off) or 24–48. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**EM-7 — The beam changes only on committed state.** `toggle_beam` is owned by Emitter State and fixed by the Controller (PC-5, PC-2): `actor` = the seat's beam emitter id, `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source = emitter.state` (kernel CR-7: the authority check keys `(emitter.state, beam_id)`, so a beam id never matches a Body actor id or a deployable's emitter id held under another key) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, origin `PLAYER`. The payload carries no state (it is a toggle: the `beam_toggle` press flips `switch_on`), so a rejected or duplicated command can never desynchronise the intent. Its apply flips `switch_on` in P2 of tick T; `emitter.place` in P3 of the same tick computes `output_pm`; the committed light therefore changes in the tick the toggle applies, with zero internal latency. The click and the hand's switch animation pre-play immediately (Presenter); **the light changes only on committed state and the Presenter never predicts beam state** (PC-5), because the beam is the human-channel anchor and may never lie, not even for one flicker. The seat's beam id is allocated by E9 inside the new-game LOADING (the Emitter's `init_world` step, or the session owner's new-game step under the same `WriteScope`, before the kernel's rebuild); the Emitter registers a **kernel binding source** at BOOTING (kernel CR-7): `beam_bindings() -> [(player_id, beam_id)]`, ascending `player_id`, a pure read of `emitter.state`; the kernel's LOADING rebuild binds each pair after every `post_restore()` (new game included), which is what lets `toggle_beam` carry `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`. The binding table is not saved (CR-7) and is rebuilt from `beam_bindings()` after every restore (EM-28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *Alternative considered:* the Controller allocates the beam id — rejected (CR-8). **Strobe protection is a sim guard, owned here** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; this supersedes the first-draft orchestrator ruling that routed the whole concern to the Controller's Adapter)*: the Adapter's debounce (`BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS`, owner Player Controller & Input, registry, PC-5) covers only the local human submitter, and PC-5 and Controller Open Question 18 both state that the sim-side guard "is Emitter State's to add"; with no guard here a replayed, scripted or remote submitter bypasses it and Suit SE-35's drain-sampling protection (the six-tick window) and the WCAG 2.3.1 limit rest on one client. The beam record therefore carries a canonical `last_toggle_tick` (EM-4), and `toggle_beam.validate` rejects `TOO_SOON` when `last_toggle_tick ≥ 0` and `T − last_toggle_tick < SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` (12 commit ticks, owned by this GDD, derived in D.2b; it replaces the first draft's citation of the Adapter's `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` as the sim's threshold, and the Adapter constant now sits at or above it); the apply of an accepted toggle writes `last_toggle_tick = T`. *Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D32):* the same **commit-spacing rule** applies to `set_switch` for every submitter and every origin (the DOCK_STATUS glow is switched by E10, not by `set_switch`, and is exempt *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), see below. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The first-draft rationale ("a sim-side `COOLDOWN` would be wall-clock-shaped") was wrong: the field is counted in ticks, is canonical, and is therefore deterministic and save-equivalent. The guard applies in both directions (a turn-OFF inside the window is also `TOO_SOON`; the rule that a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge, EM-10, is about charge, not rate); `force_off` (Suit, the DEAD tick) is not a `toggle_beam` and neither reads nor writes the field. The validate order is `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `TOO_SOON`, `CHARGE_EMPTY`. An Adapter-compliant stream is never rejected **only if** `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` is at least `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`: the Adapter's registry value is 10 today, so until the Player Controller raises it to 12 (its range 10–20 allows it; 2D Lighting Ask E-E proposes the same) a human stream pressing every 10 ticks has every second press refused `TOO_SOON` (no light change, no charge drain); this is listed under I-SPACING (D.15) and AC-90b, not hidden. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**EM-9 — The beam in every actionable state; DOWNED keeps it, DEAD ends it.** The beam is available while the actor is IDLE, WALK, RUN, CARRY_WALK or CHANNELLING (PC-8; the user's chest-lamp decision: nothing the hands do touches the lamp). While `loco_state == DOWNED` the beam keeps its committed state — the aim is frozen at the last committed value and the origin is the `chest_sim` of the down animation row; a downed crewmate is a locator (P1) — which is the handoff PC left to this GDD ("Emitter State decides what a downed emitter does"). While STAGGERED the state is likewise unchanged. At the tick `emitter.place` reads `loco_state == DEAD`, it forces `switch_on` false (the Controller's `DEAD` row: "beam off (Emitter State on actor death)") as an `emitter.place`-internal `force_off`, a read of `controller.state` with no command. Because Save/Load's death stub restarts from the last autosave through `request_restore` at that tick's P6, the DEAD-tick off-state is unobservable in the MVP (say so in tests). A beam that stays on over a corpse until Suit's charge runs out — a corpse as a lantern the web can see — is *not* a rule here; it is a VS-B question for Attention and Sanity (Open Questions). In IN_POD the beam follows its actor into the pod's body frame (EM-30; Ship Body's `body_of_actor` carries the frame and Web Map & Transit is designed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**EM-10 — Beam charge is Suit's.** Suit & Equipment owns charge, drain, `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the HUD "beam and tool charge" reading (art bible HUD set). `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's charge view and rejects a turn-ON at zero charge with `CHARGE_EMPTY`; a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge (the strobe floor `TOO_SOON` of EM-7 applies to both directions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Suit's divisor-6 `suit.vitals` reads `emitter.state.lit` on the seat's beam to drain charge and calls `force_off(beam_id)` (E5) at zero; because `suit.vitals` runs earlier in the tick than `emitter.place`, a `force_off` takes effect in the same tick's `emitter.place`, and the owner's six-tick re-check (EM-25) then finds a channelled target unlit and aborts, so at most five ticks of channel run on a dark target. The beam is a *suit load, not a ship LOAD*: Emitter State never calls `set_load_request` for it and the Graph is not involved. (Suit & Equipment, designed: SE-8; Suit keeps the hook name `suit.vitals` and its `after: graph.propagate.atmo`.)

**EM-11 — Fixtures are switchable Graph LOADs; the lamp formula gates on the switch.** A FIXTURE carries `node_ref` (a Graph `13 LOAD` node of the LOAD subtype `LAMP` — the Item DB assigns the subtype id, currently `2 LAMP`; the Graph names only `HEATER`; provisional), `base_pm` (from the def's `emits`) and `switch_on`. Its brightness is `lamp_output_pm` (Formulas D.1): `output_pm = switch_on and armed and live ? ⌊base_pm * served_pm / 1000⌋ : 0`. The lit branch is the registry formula `power_allocation`'s output "lamp brightness = base * served_pm / 1000", reused verbatim. **`served_pm` is the tier's satisfaction `sat_k`, independent of the node's own request** (Graph D.6), so a switched-off lamp can still read `served_pm` 1000: the Emitter's own `switch_on` is the gate, not the Graph, or an off lamp would shine. Power draw is a Graph LOAD: inside the `set_switch` apply the Emitter calls M14 `set_load_request(node_ref, req_w)` with `req_w` the def's rated draw (Graph MVP: 20 W) when on and 0 when off (Class B: it clamps to `0..req_max`, queues to the next Graph phase 0, and is a no-op on an unknown, tombstoned, dormant or SALVAGED node). A lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (Graph P1); under re-energise inrush the bank draws `req_w * INRUSH_PM / 1000` for `INRUSH_STEPS` runs, which can dim the tier-3 bank for half a second — the Graph's business, visible as an honest dip, changing no Emitter rule. The Emitter never recomputes watts and never calls M14 for node lanterns or the beam. A FIXTURE with `node_ref` 0 is *self-powered*: permitted only for the two declared subkinds, EMERGENCY (the cryo-bay emergency lamp, exactly one in the world, declared by Derelict Authoring DA-23 as `fixture_subkind_emergency`) and DOCK_STATUS (below); it has no M14 call, no ARMING and a fixed `base_pm`, and any other `node_ref` 0 fixture is refused by the authoring lint and at boot (`SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`: exactly one EMERGENCY, exactly one DOCK_STATUS per dock room, none elsewhere). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; second subkind added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)* **The DOCK_STATUS fixture (user ruling X2, 2026-10-27)** keeps the pod console's lit gate satisfied at every dock without a further `act_gate` exception *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (Interaction's IA-6 refusal of a `pod_hop` exemption stands): it is an *ordinary lit fixture* (`gates_actions` true, SOFT curve, counted in `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `section_emission`, so the web can read it like any lamp, P3 and "light is never free"), authored by Derelict Authoring on the dock room's docked-podcraft prop, in the **dock room's section** and not on the pod body (the pod section is dormant always, Web Map WM-5, and the lamp must not depend on it). It is created and discarded with its section (E1, E2), has no `node_ref` and therefore no liveness test (EM-13 concerns Graph nodes) and cannot be failed, starved or drained by any ship state, which is the point: the stranded player always finds the console lit. Its `switch_on` is driven only by the mutator **E10 `set_dock_status(section_id, on)`**, which Web Map & Transit calls in the apply that writes `pod_at` (on for the dock room the pod parks at, off for the one it leaves; the berth and unberth verbs are the derelict weld verbs and have nothing to do with it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the first draft named the berth and unberth applies, and read `pod_at` at E1)*, so the glow emits only while the pod is there. **E1 creates every DOCK_STATUS glow switched off and reads nothing of Web Map's state**: E1 runs at `init_world` step 2, before Web Map writes `pod_at` at step 7, so the home dock's glow is switched on by Web Map's step-7 call to E10 (`pod_at` HOME) in the same `init_world` apply, and the derelict docks' glows stay off until the pod parks there. `set_switch` of either origin is refused `NOT_SWITCHABLE` for this subkind and Interaction registers no switch interactable for it; it takes no M14 call and no ARMING, and E10 has no commit-spacing guard and writes no `last_toggle_tick` (E10's row in EM-5 gives the reason: the pod's own timing spaces the transitions, and an atomic apply could not observe a refusal) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Values** (placeholders, owner game-designer and art-director, confirmed by the Lighting spike; derivation in D.1b): `DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` 500, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX` 48, shape row 7 (`FIXTURE`, SOFT) at that reach, and the placement constraint `DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX` 24 (the console subject's anchor lies within 24 px of the glow origin, clear of every occluder). Its luminance and hue sit outside the visible-unknown lamp's band (the art-director's, not this GDD's; a Lighting `hue_class` token owed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**EM-12 — One latency story for switching.** A `set_switch` applies at P2 of tick `T_a`; its M14 call is queued to the next Graph phase 0; the lamp is **ARMING with `output_pm` 0** until `arm_tick`, the first `graph.propagate.power` run that consumed the request, and is lit on the first `emitter.place` at or after it (Formulas D.2 `switch_latency`: `arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`). Under the stated assumptions the lamp is lit between 0 and `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks after the apply — at most 83 ms — and no single number from this paragraph is a design fact: D.2 derives the range with a worked example at both alignments (switch on a Graph tick; switch on the tick after one). **Assumption A1 (derived, not assumed; confirmed by the Graph 2026-10-27 in its Interactions row for this system):** kernel CR-2 ("P3 sees all of P2") and Graph LS-8 phase 0 ("apply queued unconditional inputs: `set_load_request` changes") together mean that an M14 call made in P2 of a Graph tick is consumed by that same tick's phase 0, so the range is 0..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks; the negative case, a Graph that applied only strictly later requests, would give 1..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` and is kept in D.2 as the labelled alternative. The direct `after: graph.propagate.failure` entry (EM-1) guarantees that the hook reads that run's output on the same tick. Switching **off** is immediate (`output_pm` 0 from the apply tick; M14 `(node_ref, 0)`); an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels the pending ON and is not a realised transition (it writes no `last_toggle_tick`, EM-7, D.2b). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32)* The same "light changes only on committed state" rule PC-5 states for the beam holds for fixtures; the asymmetry (ON waits for the Graph pulse, OFF does not) is deliberate and physical: the ship has to serve the lamp, and the lamp cannot go on ahead of the ship. Fixtures never pre-play light; the wall-switch click and animation pre-play. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

218	**EM-13 — Liveness: a lamp is dark when its node is dead.** A lamp or lantern is *live* iff its `node_ref` exists and `node(id).state` is neither `3 DESTROYED`, `2 FAILED`, `4 SALVAGED` nor `5 ABSENT` (Graph LS-10) and the node is not dormant or tombstoned (read each tick from the Graph read view). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: 'live' is the output rule only. Command validation uses 'structurally present' (EM-7), which excludes SALVAGED, ABSENT, dormant and tombstoned nodes but not FAILED or DESTROYED ones, so a failed lamp can still be switched.)* A not-live lamp has `output_pm` 0 while its `switch_on` stays as committed — when the node is repaired the lamp lights again without a new command. `served_pm` and node `state` are read live each tick; both change only on Graph ticks, and because `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (EM-1) a Graph-tick read sees the state the run just produced, never a pre-failure-phase state. Which Graph states count as "running" for a *lantern* is the Item DB's `lantern_on_states` (default `{0 OK, 1 DEGRADED}`, resolved 2026-10-26). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(orchestrator ruling: R22 as amended at the checkpoint (CP-3) — `emitter.place` declares the direct `after:` entry, so no read is ever lagged; the technical-director's proposal to sample slow inputs once per Graph run into canonical state is not adopted, because the direct ordering needs no sampled state and a restore at a Graph tick rebuilds the identical table.)*

220	**EM-14 — Node lanterns are derived and switchless.** A NODE_LANTERN stands for the glow of a running machine (every machine node whose def carries an `emits` with shape `LANTERN`; the kinds are Item DB data, IDB-31, not a list in this rule: in the MVP a reactor cell, a coolant pump and a scrubber). E1 creates one NODE_LANTERN per such node, and nothing in this rule restricts the kind; the shape key stays `LANTERN` and the hue is per loop (`LANTERN_POWER`, `LANTERN_COOLANT`, `LANTERN_O2`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* It has no switch and makes no `set_load_request` call: `output_pm` is `⌊base_pm * term / 1000⌋` when the node is live and *running* (Formulas D.3 `node_lantern_output`), where `term` is the node's `run_pm` reading. A lantern gated on `served_pm` alone would glow from a switched-off machine (the same trap as EM-11), so the lantern reads a *running* quantity `run_pm` from the Graph read view — **delivered by the Graph** (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27: `node(id).run_pm`, 0..1000 — 0 when the requested load is 0 (LOAD `req_w` 0, PUMP `throttle_pm` 0, REACTOR `out_w` 0), otherwise `served_pm` for a consumer and `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋` for a REACTOR; it is not the Graph's D.9 `duty_pm`, which reads 1000 for a machine switched off on a met tier and carries the same trap as EM-11). The Emitter **consumes `run_pm` as published and clamps it** to 0..1000 (D.3): it never recomputes it from `out_w`, so a REACTOR running above rated output cannot make a lantern outshine its `base_pm`, and a rated output of 0 is the Graph's guard, not an Emitter division. There is no fallback form: a browned-out or starved machine glows at its served fraction and a lantern that cannot read `run_pm` is a boot defect, not a weaker rule (a lantern at full `base_pm` while its machine starves would lie about power state, P1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Lanterns are created and destroyed with their section (EM-5), counted against Lighting's lantern budget by authoring lint (EM-26), and killing the machine is the only way to dark one — "every loop you run is a lantern the web can see" (art bible Principle 3).

222	**EM-15 — Deployables and glowsticks: spawn on landing, steady, then waning, then gone.** `spawn_deployable(kind, pos_px, owner, life_ticks)` (E3) is called by Interaction's landing-tick hook (PC D.16: "the light exists only on landing"; the thrown light is never pre-played). The glowstick numbers are the Item DB's placeholders and are cited by name: `GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` 150 (60–300), `GLOWSTICK_RADIUS_TILES` 2 (= 96 base px, 1.5–3), `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` 4, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 400, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM` 250 (Item DB IDB-12). No tick-denominated life constant is registered by this GDD: the record's `life_total_ticks` is `ticks_for_seconds(GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S)` = 9000 taken from the def at spawn, and the Item DB's rule that **the life is counted from the throw tick, not from landing** (a stick that never lands still burns out) is honoured by Interaction passing `life_ticks` = the life remaining at landing (9000 minus `THROW_ARC_TICKS` 30 for a thrown stick). This GDD owns the curve's *semantics*, id `WANE_LINEAR_25`: while the remaining life fraction is at or above `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM / 1000` the emitter holds its full reach (steady); below it, `reach_px` falls linearly (in the permille factor `f`, then floored to whole px) to `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM / 1000` of full reach at the last tick (24 px at `life_remaining_ticks` 1); this is the Item DB's F-7 `reach_px(rem)` verbatim, so the two GDDs agree tick for tick; at `life_remaining_ticks` 0 the record is removed and its id retired (Formulas D.9). *(orchestrator ruling: the Item DB's steady-then-waning parameterisation, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 400, is adopted over the routed ruling's linear-from-spawn curve — they are the same curve at `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 1000 — because the art bible specifies "steady at full value, then dimming monotonically", and the Item DB owns these numbers. A different number there is a conflict to surface, not a silent change.)* The output stays constant (`GLOWSTICK_BASE_PM`), the reveal radius shrinks, and that waning is **sim state**, not presentation, because it changes the real reveal radius (P1). It never flickers (art bible 3.2); the flicker of the VS-A flare, torch and decoy family is Lighting's and invisible to the query, which uses the steady mean. The stick lights the floor plane in ship-local px, counts as exposure like any pool (Attention may weight by area rather than radius — a pool at the floor radius has one sixteenth of the full area; the read view carries `reach_px` and the shape so either is derivable), and a stick landing in a closed room lights only that room (occluders). At most `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` non-evicting deployables exist. **Cap eviction is a visible wane, never an instant removal** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 2: a light dying with no physical cause would break the promise that a stick's waning is its only clock, and would be a P1 lie)*: a spawn over the cap (Class B never rejects; the item was already spent, and Item DB rule (c): a landed stick is spent without refund) is applied in full, and the lowest-id deployable of the same kind that is not already evicting enters an **evict-wane** — `evict_tick` and `reach_at_evict` are written, its output stays `GLOWSTICK_BASE_PM`, and its reach falls linearly from its current reach to the 24 px floor over `ticks_for_seconds(GLOWSTICK_EVICT_WANE_S)` ticks (placeholder 10 s = 600 ticks, owner game-designer, Tuning Knobs), then the record is removed and its id retired (Formulas D.9b). It reads in the world as a stick guttering fast, the same visible monotone shrink as the ordinary wane, only quicker; the 24 px floor is the ordinary wane's own last value, so the final removal is the same event the ordinary end of life already is. An evicting stick still exposes, still gates actions and still sums at its current reach until it is gone; it does not count against `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE`, but the evicting tail is itself bounded by `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` (placeholder 4); an eviction that would exceed it completes the oldest evicting stick at once, increments `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow` and fires a debug assertion — a budget defect, never a gameplay state. **Eviction is meant to be unreachable by supply in the MVP, and that supply bound belongs to other owners** *(cross-GDD invariant I-SUPPLY, routed, Cross-References; the total glowsticks one seat carries across all stacks is at most `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE`, so no seat can have more sticks in flight than the cap)*: Suit & Equipment owns the per-seat carry count and start count, the Item DB owns `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX`, and Derelict Authoring owns the loose-stick supply by depth, which must not allow a throw-pickup-throw cycle to exceed the cap inside one `GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` (a landed stick is never picked up again, Item DB rule (c), so a cycle needs a loose stick on the floor). The evict-wane exists because the bound can be violated by content and by VS-B (four seats × a stack of 4 is 16 against a cap of 8); every eviction increments the release telemetry counter `emitter_deployable_evictions`.

224	**EM-16 — The beacon is a pure function of time.** A BEACON is a 20° cone (shape row 8) whose axis is `beacon_aim = (beacon_phase + beacon_dir * ⌊T * AIM_UNITS / BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS⌋) mod 4096` with `T` the kernel clock tick (non-negative modulus), `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (2.13 s, inside the art bible's 2–3 s; placeholder, owner art-director / audio, confirmed by the Lighting spike), so the step is exactly 32 units per tick. Direction and phase are authored data; **no per-tick angle state exists**, which is what makes save-equivalence automatic (the kernel clock is persisted by the kernel). *(orchestrator ruling: the rational form of the systems-designer over the routed ruling's `T * BEACON_UNITS_PER_TICK`, because it is identical at 128 and lets any integer sweep length be valid — the ruled range 120–180 contained exactly one divisor of 4096.)* The beacon's brightness is the lamp formula when it carries a `node_ref` (MVP: it does — a dead ship's beacon is dark, P1), switched by `set_beacon`; turned on, it starts from the angle the pure function gives at that tick (no restart at phase 0). It is a dynamic-layer emitter (it rotates) and `gates_actions` is **false** *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's F9 adopted, then **ruled kept by the user 2026-10-27 (Open Question 1, D20; no longer provisional)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* — a cone sweeping over a point lights it for 14 or 15 of every 128 ticks by phase (the cone is 456 units wide and the sweep advances 32 units per tick, so ⌊456/32⌋ = 14 or ⌈456/32⌉ = 15; about 11 %), and a prompt that strobes at the sweep rate, or a channel that aborts every 128 ticks, would be the system lying about what can be worked; the beacon exposes and is seen, it does not enable verbs. This narrows the Controller's PC-6 for one kind; routed to the technical-director and game-designer)*.

226	**EM-17 — Fault glow is a derived emitter kind.** FAULT_GLOW emitters stand for a venting ember, a power arc and cyan O₂ mist as point sources (art bible 2.8 / Failure & Trail). They are created and removed by `emitter.place` from the Graph's failure descriptors (`failures(filter)`), each keyed by `FailureDescriptor.mode` (a failure mode 1..10, or a descriptor-only id 20..26) plus `medium`, matching the Failure & Trail glow-table keys; the MVP rows with a glow are `1/FUEL`, `1/GAS`, `2`, `3`, `7`, `9`. They use Failure & Trail's descriptor-to-glow data table (rows owned by F&T; a descriptor with no glow row creates no emitter), by comparing the Graph's list, read on Graph ticks, against the FAULT_GLOW records that already exist — no subscription (kernel CR-10) and no stored previous list. They have no switch, no Graph LOAD and no command; `output_pm` comes from the descriptor's `sev` 0..4 and the row's `sev_min` gate (D.11); they are non-shadow and count as exposure. **Position, section and frame — the anchor rule** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft read mode, medium and `sev` from the descriptor but no position, and the Graph has no pixel geometry (LS-19), so the cone and radius test, the occlusion start `S`, the `section_emission` attribution and sim/render agreement had nothing to stand on)*: a FAULT_GLOW record's position is read from Layout, never guessed. For a descriptor that has a glow row: (1) `section_id` = the Graph's `section_of(descriptor.anchor)` — `section_of(node_id)` for a `(node_id, port_local_index)` anchor, `section_of(edge_id)` for an `edge_id` anchor (a compartment descriptor has no anchor and, by the F&T table, no glow row); (2) `body_id` = Layout `body_of(section_id)` (a Class 1 static query, valid straight after `restore()`, Layout LY-26 b); (3) `anchor_px` = **the first point, `base_px_polyline[0]`, of Layout's `anchor_geometry(descriptor.anchor)`** — the head of the combined wall-then-floor run, which is the source stamp the trail's glow comes from (FT-13, FT-27): a section-local base-px floor-plane point; for a `WALL_FACE` anchor it is the base of the host face, the first legal row in front of the wall (Layout LY-8 b), which already satisfies the clearance of EM-20 (b); and `origin_px` (derived) = `anchor_px + section_offset(section_id)` in the body frame, used for reach, distance and the occlusion start alike (EM-6: other kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both). `anchor_geometry` is a pure static read made once at creation and again in `post_restore`, never per tick. **Fallback when the Layout read is empty** (Layout returns nothing, without an error, only for a DISCARDED section, LY-23): no record is created on that Graph tick, `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor` increments (release telemetry) and a debug assertion fires; reconciliation retries on the next Graph tick, and the case cannot persist for a loaded section because Layout's lint (`WALL_FITTING_NO_RUN`, AC-87) refuses a glow-capable fitting with no run. **Clearance lint, extended to every emitter anchor** (EM-20 b): a data-load lint checks the anchor of every authored FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN and BEACON placement (the E1 input) and the head of every glow-capable `anchor_geometry` polyline against `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` for every `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangle, and refuses the build (`EMITTER_ANCHOR_CLEARANCE`, naming the placement or anchor); it covers template data, so no run-time nudge exists. If a defect gets past it, E1 or the FAULT_GLOW creation still makes the record (the exposure stays honest: `section_emission` counts it, P3) but increments `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail` and asserts in debug, and the emitter lights nothing in its own room (its segment starts inside a rectangle, so every pair is blocked) — a diagnosable defect, where the first draft's was silent. They are capped at `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` (placeholder 10); **a fault's light never goes dark with no physical cause** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 1: a real failure whose light vanishes weakens P1, the physical consequence becomes invisible, and P2, a fault glow is one of the tells a careful player reads)*, so the cap is a content bound that is held by a boot invariant (I-CAPS (c), D.15: `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` is at least the most simultaneous glowing authored faults on one body plus a 25 % margin; in the MVP slice a welded body carries at most 6 simultaneous glow rows, so the floor is ⌈1.25 × 6⌉ = 8 ≤ 10, the 8 live faults being spread world-wide across bodies; registry: `mvp_fault_allocation`), and eviction is a last resort with three rules. (1) **Lowest severity first**: when reconciliation would hold more than `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` records, the records evicted are those with the lowest `sev`, ties broken by the higher descriptor id first (the kept set is the same as "highest `sev` wins, ties by ascending descriptor id"). (2) **A protected record is never evicted**: a record whose age `T − placed_tick` is below `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)` (the Graph's registered fairness constant, 10 s = 600 ticks; cited, not restated) is protected, so the tell of a new fault is always shown for at least the Graph's warning window. (3) **Protection beats the cap**: if every candidate for eviction is protected, no record is evicted and the table stays over `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` (bounded only by `MAX_EMITTERS`, at which the creation rule of EM-24 refuses and counts), increments the release telemetry counter `emitter_fault_glow_overcap` and fires a debug assertion; it is trimmed back by rules 1 and 2 on the first Graph tick on which a candidate is no longer protected. Overcap is a content or budget defect and never a gameplay state. Every eviction increments `emitter_fault_glow_evictions`. An evicted glow removes only the descriptor's light and its exposure: the Failure & Trail emissive overlay on the sprite (an unshaded overlay, not an emitter) still draws the fault, so the fault stays visible in the world. **Timing (R22 as amended, CP-3):** `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure`, so on a Graph tick it reads the descriptor list that run just produced and a glow appears on the Graph tick of its descriptor, never later; between Graph ticks the list cannot change. A FAULT_GLOW record is a normal record (it has an id from the canonical counter), so it persists as the set of descriptors it stood for. The emissive `_msk` trail glow on a sprite is an *unshaded overlay, not an emitter*, and exposes nothing: a lit-but-unregistered source would light a room Attention cannot see (Failure & Trail's brief). Whether a glow gates actions: yes (an arc lights the scrubber beside it). (Failure & Trail's designed FT-27 agrees: it supplies "a descriptor-to-glow data table (palette hex, radius in base px, flicker class bounded by FT-29)" and "Emitter State registers the emitter from the same descriptor". **Failure & Trail owns the glow-table rows including the ledger values `GLOW_BASE_PM[key]` and `SEV_GLOW_PM[0..4]` (placeholders it carries in V/A.6); this GDD owns D.11, the FAULT_GLOW record, `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` and `FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX`, and multiplies the ledger values.** This GDD takes each row's `reach_px` from the F&T `radius_px` at the sev 4 column (the sev 3 column where sev 4 is n/a), defaulting to `FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX` when a row carries none; a row radius outside [`REACH_MIN_PX`, `REACH_MAX_PX`] (invariant I-REACH, D.15) is a data defect — the data-load lint refuses it, and if one gets past the lint the record uses `FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX`, `emitter_reach_invalid` increments and a debug assertion fires, so the glow is never dark and no division by a zero reach can occur. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* F&T's emissive layer "casts no light", which is the `_msk` sentence above.)
227	
228	**EM-18 — The illumination model: contribution, curve classes, saturating sum.** For one emitter and one subject, the contribution `c` is **0** unless all of: the subject's `body_id` equals the emitter's (EM-30), the subject is inside the emitter's radius (`d2 <= reach_px²`, a closed edge), inside its cone for cone shapes (EM-19), not blocked (EM-20). The one exception is the owner's own beam on the owner's ACTOR subject, which contributes its apex value, facing- and occlusion-independent (EM-21). For every other pair `c = ⌊output_pm * f(d, reach_px) / 1000⌋` (Formulas D.7), `d` the exact integer floor of the distance from the emitter's origin (the chest, for the beam). Two **curve classes** are carried as a data table so the Lighting spike can replace a curve without changing the API: **SOFT** (pools, fixtures, glowsticks, lanterns, fault glow) `f = 1000 * (R - d) / R`, linear to zero at the fade-out radius; **HARD** (the cones and the beacon) `f = EDGE_FLOOR_PM + (1000 - EDGE_FLOOR_PM) * (R - d) / R`, so the contribution at the rim of a full-output hard-edged emitter is `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` (placeholder 250 permille, range 160–400, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike) and the lit boundary **is** the drawn hard edge. *(orchestrator ruling: this is a deliberate deviation from the routed ruling's single default curve `c = output_pm * (R - d) / R`, which contradicts its own "hard outer edge exactly at `reach_px`" clause: with `LIT_ON_PM` 150 a full-output wide beam of reach 288 px would be actionable only to `d <= 244` px — 44 px, almost a full tile, inside the hard edge the player sees, the light visibly falling on a valve the hand cannot reach, which is the game lying (P1) and contradicts art bible hero #1. Three specialists converged on the edge-floor remedy; rejected: lowering `LIT_ON_PM` toward 0 (a near-black pixel becomes actionable — a different lie, and hysteresis dies) and redefining the "drawn edge" as an iso-line at 150 permille (contradicts the hard edge). Surfaced as a deviation from the ruling's default in the return value, not a registry conflict.)* The consequence is intended: a *dimmed* hard-edged emitter (output below `⌈LIT_ON_PM * 1000 / EDGE_FLOOR_PM⌉` = 600) has an honestly smaller actionable area; a full-output emitter is actionable to its last pixel (invariant I-EDGE: `BEAM_BASE_PM * EDGE_FLOOR_PM >= 1000 * LIT_ON_PM`). For SOFT classes the actionable radius `r_lit` is **the largest `d` whose integer chain (D.7) gives `c ≥ LIT_ON_PM`**, published by the sim per emitter as `r_lit_px` (the closed form ⌊R × (output_pm − LIT_ON_PM) / output_pm⌋ of the first draft ran 1 px high for some dimmed outputs and is not used) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, inside the fade-out radius `reach_px` by design (a full fixture of reach 144 px is actionable to 122 px on approach). The **latch-release radius** `r_off_px` (the largest `d` whose chain gives `c ≥ LIT_OFF_PM`, D.7; 126 px for the same fixture) is where an already-lit subject stops being lit: Lighting draws a soft pool to the published `r_off_px` (a prompt never appears outside the visible pool), and `r_lit_px` is where an approaching subject first becomes actionable, `r_off_px − r_lit_px` px inside the drawn edge; the Lighting spike confirms the drawn edge (the art bible and Item DB "radius" numbers — 3 tiles, 2 tiles — are provisional, and the spike must decide whether they mean fade-out or readable radius). **Resolved 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix (G6): the pool is drawn to the latch-release radius (Lighting's `soft_pool_scale`, the registry source, wins); Emitter State's `lit` latch is unchanged.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **Aggregation is a saturating sum**, `lux_pm = min(1000, Σ c)`: integer addition is commutative, so no iteration-order dependence; several lamps in one room read brighter and expose more until fully lit. There is **no ambient term**: `AMBIENT_PM` is fixed at 0 in the sim, and Lighting's ambient is cosmetic and can never make an object actionable (P1; art bible Principle 1: unlit, not fogged). `lux_pm` sums every emitter (Horror reads it; Attention reads `emitters()` and never `lux_pm`, AT-4); `act_lux_pm` sums only the emitters whose `gates_actions` is true (EM-3) and feeds `lit` (EM-22).
229	
230	**EM-19 — Cone membership is fixed-point and mirror-symmetric.** A cone test uses no trigonometry, square root or float at run time (Graph LS-1(b) precedent). Directions come from a table `DIR` of Q14 unit vectors — **the table is generated at build time by a data tool outside `src/sim/emitter/` and checked in as an integer data file, never computed in the sim module** (the boot step only loads it and asserts I-MIRROR and I-OVERFLOW, so the AC-2 lint holds) — indexed by an `AIM_UNITS` angle (0 = E, counter-clockwise, screen y down, so aim 3072 = S is `(0, +16384)`), generated from one quadrant by reflection so that `DIR[2048 - a] = (-ux, uy)` **exactly**. A subject at offset `r = anchor - origin` is in the cone iff `d2 <= R²`, `D > 0` and `D² >= d2 * COS2_Q28`, with `D = rx*ux + ry*uy` (Formulas D.5); the `D > 0` guard is required (the squared test alone accepts the opposite half-plane) and `d2 = 0` is inside every cone of that emitter, the apex included. The split beam is two tests at axes `aim ± 206` units; the wedge between them never closes (I-WEDGE), so a point is in at most one cone and its contribution is never doubled. Every product has a documented bound under 2^62 and the boot assertion refuses a build that violates it (Formulas D.15). The half-angles and the 18° offset are not integral in `AIM_UNITS`, so the shape table (EM-8) carries the encoded integers; the quantisation misplaces a rim by under 0.1° (under 0.7 px at 384 px), far inside the accepted committed-versus-drawn divergence. **The symmetry property is a test, not a hope**: the exposure of a mirrored scene (x → -x, aim `a` → `2048 - a`, `flip_h` toggled) equals the mirror image of the original exactly, for the five drawn and three mirrored facings, every `CHEST_POINT` animation row and all four shapes (Acceptance Criteria).

232	**EM-20 — Occlusion is integer geometry over the Layout's opaque footprints.** *(orchestrator ruling R3 — the one deliberate deviation from a routed thread's wording.)* The routed thread and the index describe occlusion as tests on "physics shapes".
