**EM-26 — Dirty keys, the Lighting contract and the budget agreement.** Dirty keys are emitted for **emitters**, never for individual subjects (publish rule): a key `E/<emitter id>` — an int `(KIND << 32) | id` as in Graph LS-20 — fires on create, remove, `switch_on` flip, `shape_id` change, an `output_pm` change that crosses a bucket (`OUTPUT_DIRTY_QUANTUM_PM`, placeholder 50) and an integer `reach_px` step; continuous pose (origin, aim) never dirties — Lighting polls the read view at render rate, and keys wake only discrete presentation (a light switching on or off, a record spawning). Subject `lux` and `lit` are poll reads: sim consumers read inside their hook, presentation prompts poll at render rate, so a sweeping beam over 192 subjects cannot collapse notifications to `ALL` against `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 (worst case here is every emitter, at most `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, in one tick). **The Lighting contract** (2D Lighting & Occlusion reads and never writes): per emitter `{id, kind, subkind, shape_id, origin_px, aim_units, half_angle_units, reach_px, r_lit_px, r_off_px, curve_class, output_pm, hue_class, lit, section_id, body_id, priority}` plus the shape table (`r_lit_px` and `r_off_px` are the sixteenth and seventeenth fields, the former added by the 2026-10-27 design review and the latter by the 2026-10-28 cross-GDD fix; 2D Lighting's "15-field" wording is refreshed, Cross-References). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **The foot spill is published by a separate accessor** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the 17-field record describes a stored emitter and cannot represent the spill (a sub-contribution of the BEAM record centred on the foot, EM-6). `beam_spill(beam_id)` returns, while the beam is on and `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0, the derived record `{beam_id, kind BEAM, shape_id 11, origin_px (the foot origin `occ_origin`), reach_px (`BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX`), r_lit_px (the D.7 chain), r_off_px (the same chain at `LIT_OFF_PM`), curve_class SOFT, output_pm (`BEAM_SPILL_PM`), hue_class (the beam's), section_id, body_id, priority (the owning beam's, BEAM default 255)}` and null otherwise; it is not a record, has no id of its own and is **not in `emitters()`** (so `section_emission`, Attention's list and the 96-record cap never see it), and its changes dirty the beam's own key `E/<beam id>`. Its `kind` is the owning beam's BEAM and its `priority` is the beam's (255 by default), so it is never cut before occlusion and never demoted (Ask E-L accepted 2026-10-28); it is read by Lighting only through `beam_spill(beam_id)`, it is a row of `shapes()` (row 11, conditional) but not of `emitters()`. Lighting draws the pool from its `origin_px` and `r_off_px` (edge) and `r_lit_px` (approach prompt), and the build lint of AC-56 checks the drawn edge against max(`r_off_px`, `POOL_RESIDUAL_PX`) ± 1 px (`POOL_RESIDUAL_PX` is Lighting's, 8 px) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, which is what lets "what you see lit is what the sim calls lit" be tested for the spill (AC-46c). This block publishes facts; Lighting conforms to them. Lighting owns textures, ambient, the canvas modulate, shadow-slot assignment (the sixth slot), the flash clamp (`flash_count` ≤ 3 per rolling second per light), flicker, gutter and decoy visuals; flicker is invisible to the query, which uses the steady mean. **Budget agreement (R17):** the sim never culls by view (an off-screen emitter still exposes — correct for P3); instead authoring lint keeps in-view emitter counts under Lighting's hypotheses (shadow-casting ≤ 6, non-shadow ≤ 24, node lanterns ≤ 8; art bible 8.10 budget shape and 8.11 flags 2 and 8), a debug assertion reports overflow, and every record carries a deterministic `priority` (default by kind: BEAM 255, BEACON 200, FIXTURE 120, DEPLOYABLE 100, FAULT_GLOW 80, NODE_LANTERN 60 — placeholder, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike) so Lighting's "emitters are cut before occlusion" is reproducible; a sim-lit but unrendered light would be a P1 lie, and the residual risk stays in Open Questions. A build lint asserts the rendered reach of every hard-edged row equals the table reach ±1 px.

**EM-27 — The light stimulus for Attention.** The primary read is the per-emitter list (`emitters()`: id, kind, `section_id`, `body_id`, origin, `output_pm`, `reach_px`, shape); the convenience read is `section_emission(section_id)` (Formulas D.12). Attention owns units and weights. The stimulus is **shape-blind by design** (D.12: a narrow beam reads about 2.3 times louder than the fan; default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **No double counting:** the Graph's `power_use(section_id).lamps_lit_w` is the *power* stimulus; this block's `output_pm`-weighted reach is the *light* stimulus; Attention must not count one lamp as both. The owner's own beam counts once, at its apex value, in the owner's `lux_pm` (EM-21); Attention reads it as emission and does not add it again. Off-screen and unoccupied emitters count. The seat's beam is attributed to the section its foot origin stands in (EM-4, Body's `actor_section`), and the attribution changes in the tick the foot crosses a door, so Attention's per-section ledger and Horror's targeting see the player's exposure where the player is. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Attention may weight a pool by area rather than radius (the list carries `reach_px` and the shape). (Attention is designed: AT-4 reads `emitters()` and no `probe()`, AT-18 concurs on the beacon.) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**EM-28 — Persistence, restore and the binding table.** *Canonical* (snapshotted, hashed): the id counter; per record, the canonical fields of EM-4 (including the FAULT_GLOW records, which are the descriptors they stand for, with their `placed_tick`, the age that protects them from eviction; `arm_tick`; a beam's `last_toggle_tick` (the only source of the `TOO_SOON` strobe guard, EM-7); and a deployable's `evict_tick` and `reach_at_evict`, so an evict-wane in progress survives a save); and the subject registrations (EM-21 table, canonical columns, including each subject's `lit` hysteresis bit, EM-22); no record and no subject stores `body_id` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *Derived, rebuilt in `post_restore`, never hashed:* beam origin and aim, `origin_px` / `aim_units` / `reach_px` / `output_pm` / record `lit`, every record's and every subject's `body_id` (Layout `body_of`; Body `body_of_actor` for the beam and ACTOR subjects), a beam's and an ACTOR subject's `section_id`, the per-section `static_version` cache of EM-23 W0 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, the static-layer pair rows and each subject's unsaturated raw sum, the per-tick read-view snapshot and the per-section emission array (EM-25), and the subject `lux_pm` / `act_lux_pm` / `top_emitter_id` table (the subject's `lit` bit is not rebuilt: it is kept). A snapshot taken before a weld and restored into a Layout that is already welded (Layout restores first, `restore_after`) yields body ids from Layout, never from the snapshot *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Rejected: `persist false` (`switch_on`, `life_remaining_ticks`, `arm_tick` and the beacon's data have no other source, so save-equivalence would break). `post_restore` runs after all blocks restore (CR-8) and rebuilds the derived set in ascending id, including the whole static layer (the cold class of D.14, scenario S6, so that no subject is pending when the first `validate` runs); the block does not run its hook while RESTORING. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The kernel does not state that `post_restore` calls follow `restore_after`, while Layout re-derives door leaves in its own `post_restore` (Layout LY-26 c): the Emitter's cold build is only correct for open doors if Layout's runs first, so the ordering is requested of the kernel (Open Question 26) and, until it is granted, the restore-time version bump of the narrowing rule (EM-23) re-tests the leaf pairs on tick 1. After a restore the kernel's binding table is rebuilt: the kernel's LOADING rebuild re-binds the seat beams from `beam_bindings()` before the first RUNNING tick (KRN-BIND-01), so there is no window in which `toggle_beam` meets an empty table *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Save-equivalence (kernel G4) holds with no accepted exception: the `lit` bit is canonical (EM-22), and the hook is ordered after the Graph's last hook on a Graph tick (EM-1). It also depends on one **requirement on the Graph**, now met: its `post_restore` rebuilds `served_pm` and the descriptor list from restored canonical state (Graph LS-21 and its restore edge case, 2026-10-27; Cross-References), without which lamps would read dark and fault glows would be absent for up to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks after a load. AC-41 fails if a regression removes the rebuild. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `schema_version` 1; the restore migration policy is the owner's (kernel CR-8: an unsupported version is a reported failure, never a silent default). The block has a round-trip test (kernel CR-8) and a `state_hash` that covers the canonical set only.

**EM-29 — Isolation: the truth channel.** `emitter.state` is a `SIM` block. The module **never obtains a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view** (kernel CR-12; a lint mirroring PC's acceptance criterion on the Adapter's requested views), never references `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`, `Node` or `PhysicsServer2D` (the H10 lint over `src/sim/emitter/`), and runs under a headless test with zero scene nodes. The beam, the real reveal radius and lamp / fixture brightness are on the closed **consequence channel** (the Graph's closed consequence-channel list names "lamp brightness"; the Controller's Perception Filter row: the Filter "may never move the chest point ... or touch the beam"). **A Perception Filter decoy light is a Lighting visual**: it is not an emitter, is absent from `emitter.state`, and exposes nothing; rejected: decoys as `phantom = true` emitters (a perception fact written into a `SIM` block breaks CR-12 and H5). No sentence in this GDD says the Filter may dim, move or add a lamp. The honest cross-check — walk to the real edge and it is where it always was — depends on this. Isolation is by construction, not by policy: no field named `phantom`, `perceived` or `decoy` exists, and the query never takes a Filter-wrapped value (the Graph's `true_value` is the only wrapped path and Emitter State never calls it).

**EM-30 — Frames, zoom, mirror and the determinism contract.** All geometry is integer base px; stored anchors are **section-local** (Layout's frame, LY-3 c) and are composed with `section_offset(section_id)` once per derive, and every comparison runs in the **body frame** (ship-local); an emitter and a subject are compared only if their `body_id` matches. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The `body_id` of every emitter and subject is derived from Layout (EM-4), so all sections welded into one body share one `body_id`: light crosses a weld, the beam lights the objects of a welded derelict and its lamps count toward the player, exactly as Lighting draws it; sections that are not welded (an unwelded derelict, a docked pod) are other bodies and stay dark to each other. A subject on another body (an unwelded or cut-off section, a pod) is not lit by the home frame's emitters (cross-body light between unwelded bodies is VS-A, Open Question 9) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Zoom, camera, render scale and the integer ladder change **nothing** in the sim; an off-screen lit object stays lit and exposes, and no prompt is drawn off-screen (the HUD's rule). Light positions are integer base px at 60 Hz (`TICK_RATE`); every duration is in ticks via `ticks_for_seconds`. The determinism contract mirrors the Graph's LS-1: integer-only SIM state; **zero floats** stored, hashed, replicated or used on the query path (a designer float in a data file is converted once by `int(round(x * scale))` in the build-time data tool outside `src/sim/emitter/`, which emits the immutable integer tables — `DIR`, the EM-8 `COS2_Q28` column and the like — that the boot step loads and asserts; they are not block state, and no float or trig call exists in the sim module, AC-2); the Q14 direction table, the Q28 cone test, an exact integer floor square root and integer segment-versus-rectangle tests; no global RNG (the block draws none); iteration in ascending id; budgets in counted units; `state_hash` over the canonical set only. Physics-derived observations never enter this block, so the kernel's G3 recording obligation does not apply.

**MVP slice.** MVP (single-player): one seat beam; the home-ship's fixtures (count per room fixed by Derelict Authoring DA-22, registry `mvp_fixture_counts`: home 8, AC-58), derelict A (4 compartments) and B (5) fixtures and node lanterns; the self-powered cryo-bay emergency lamp and one self-powered DOCK_STATUS glow per dock room (X2); the beam's 24 px foot spill (D24); one alarm beacon; glowsticks (`MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8); FAULT_GLOW for the MVP faults with a glow row (`1/FUEL`, `1/GAS`, `2`, `3`, `7`, `9`). VS-A: flares, torches, decoys (`POOL_DEPLOYABLE`), more fixtures, cross-body light. VS-B: four beams, `SHARED_SUMMARY` replication, the corpse-lantern question. Nothing else in this GDD is gated.

### States and Transitions

Three small machines live in this block — the emitter record, the subject's `lit` bit and the block itself — plus one table that says what the beam does in each of the Controller's locomotion states. Every pair not listed is invalid and is reported to diagnostics (counter `emitter_invalid_transition`, labelled with the from and to states; AC-109), never silently applied. "Who may cause" is exhaustive: a transition no row names does not exist. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

**Emitter record lifecycle.** `output_pm` is 0 in every state except ON and WANING.

- Hook: `emitter.place` (divisor 1, offset 0, after [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure])
- Commands: `toggle_beam` (PLAYER), `set_switch` (PLAYER/SYSTEM), `set_beacon` (SYSTEM); domain codes `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `TOO_SOON`, `CHARGE_EMPTY`, `NOT_SWITCHABLE`, `COOLDOWN`, `NOT_LIVE`, `NOT_BEACON`
- Mutators: E1 `instantiate_section_emitters(section_id)`, E2 `discard_section_emitters(section_id)`, E3 `spawn_deployable(kind,pos_px,owner,life_ticks)`, E4 `bind_beam(player_id,shape_id)`, E5 `force_off(beam_id)`, E6 `register_subject(ref,kind,anchor_px,section_id)`, E7 `unregister_subject(ref)`, E8 `set_subject_anchor(ref,anchor_px)`, E9 `create_seat_beam(player_id)`, E10 `set_dock_status(section_id,on)`
- Kernel binding source: `beam_bindings()`
- Read view: `emitters(filter)` / `emitter(id)`, `beam_of(player_id)`, `beam_spill(beam_id)`, `lux(ref)`, `lit(ref)`, `top_emitter(ref)`, `section_emission(section_id)`, `subject_headroom()`, `emitters_near(body_id,px,r)` (provisional name), `shapes()`, `registered(ref)` (debug only); deferred to VS-A: `lit_by`, `probe`, `lit_static`
- Record field `emitter.state.lit` (emitting) vs query `lit(ref)` (exposure), kept verbatim
- Dirty keys `E/<emitter id>`
- Registry entries owned: `light_shape` (shape table, incl. row 11 BEAM_SPILL conditional), `emitter_kind`, `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`, `LIT_ON_PM`/`LIT_OFF_PM` family, `EDGE_FLOOR_PM`, `BEAM_BASE_PM`, `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX`/`BEAM_SPILL_PM`, `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192, `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` 16, `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8, `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` 10, `EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS` 0.4, `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128, `DOCK_STATUS_*`
- Release telemetry counters (`emitter_subjects_overflow`, `emitter_create_refused`, `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling`, etc.)

## Consumes

- Command & Simulation Layer (kernel): tick T, WriteScope, hook resolver, binding table, `ticks_for_seconds`, CR-3/5/8/9/10
- Life-Support Graph: `served_pm(node_id)`, `node(id)` state and `run_pm`, `failures(filter)`, `section_of`, door_state; calls M14 `set_load_request(node_id, req_w)`; hooks `graph.propagate.power/atmo/failure`
- Player Controller & Input: `controller.state` (`chest_sim`, `aim_angle`, `loco_state`, `facing`), `CHEST_POINT`; Adapter submits `toggle_beam`
- Ship ("Body") & Interior Physics: `body.state` `pos_curr`, `body_of_actor`, `actor_section`; hook `body.integrate`
- Ship Section & Layout Data Model: `OccluderSource` (`rects_in`, `version`), `body_of`, `section_offset`, `static_version`, `changed_region`, `anchor_geometry`, door-leaf projection, `occludes_light`
- Suit & Equipment: charge view (CHARGE_EMPTY), `bind_beam`/`force_off` caller, `suit.vitals` hook ordering
- Item & Module Database: `emits {shape_id, base_pm, hue_class}`, LOAD subtype LAMP, `GLOWSTICK_*`, `lantern_on_states`
- Failure & Trail: glow-table rows, `GLOW_BASE_PM[key]`, `SEV_GLOW_PM[0..4]`
- Web Map & Transit: calls E1 (init_world), E10; Derelict Authoring: placements and lints; Interaction: E3/E6-E8 callers and `lit(ref)` consumer; Attention/Horror/Lighting/Audio/HUD/Debug Overlay: read-view consumers
- Save/Load: block registration contract (SL-25)

## Engine risk

- No scene-tree, Light2D, physics or rendering API is used by the sim module (explicitly banned); LOW overall.
- GDScript typed/packed arrays (PackedInt32Array / typed Array) for sorted read-view columns and pair rows; ADR candidate 6 notes plain Dictionary cannot meet copy-free/no-allocation: LOW (long-standing), performance risk MEDIUM (GDScript op cost not sourceable from pinned engine reference; spike required).
- Integer-only math (int64 in GDScript, products < 2^62) and build-time-generated integer data files: LOW.
- Release export on Godot 4.7.2 with forward_plus renderer is the benchmark environment (AC-53): HIGH (4.5-4.7 version pin, benchmark depends on 4.7 export templates).
- Physics 2D deliberately not used (CR-13 G3 no determinism claim; 2D ray API not sourceable in pinned reference): LOW, avoided.
- Drawn counterparts (Light2D/shadows, flash governor) belong to 2D Lighting & Occlusion, which reads this system's view; the Light2D/occluder behavior spike (LO-10) gates ADR candidate 5 (foot-origin vs chest walk-back): HIGH (Lighting spike on 4.7).

# TRs: Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (alias: emitter)

Source: design/gdd/emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query.md (Status Designed, cross-GDD pass 2026-10-28)

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-emitter-001 | Emitter State is exactly one persisted SIM block `emitter.state` (persist true, scope WORLD/SHARED, repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY, schema_version 1, supported_versions [1], added_in_format 1, restore_after [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]) registered at BOOTING; boot lints refuse a block lacking supported_versions or added_in_format. | Save/Load | EM-1 |
| TR-emitter-002 | The module registers exactly one step hook `emitter.place` (divisor 1, offset 0, after [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]) doing all per-tick work in fixed order W0..W7; no second hook; in MIRROR mode the hook never runs. | Threading/Timing | EM-1, EM-23 |
| TR-emitter-003 | The module under src/sim/emitter/ is scene-tree free, integer-only, and never references Light2D, LightOccluder2D, Node or PhysicsServer2D, nor obtains a PERCEPTION_OUT view; it runs headless with zero scene nodes (enforced by lint). | Core | EM-29, EM-30 |
| TR-emitter-004 | Emitter records are created, changed and destroyed only through published mutators E1..E10 inside a kernel WriteScope by their declared callers (Class A infallible, Class B clamp/never reject); Lighting, Attention, Horror and presentation never write emitters; mutators outside a WriteScope assert in debug and reject in release. | Core | EM-5 |
| TR-emitter-005 | Emitter records have u32 ids allocated from a canonical counter inside the block, never reused, strictly ascending; all iteration is in ascending emitter id / subject ref, never Dictionary order. | Core | EM-4 |
| TR-emitter-006 | The emitter kind set is closed (BEAM, FIXTURE incl. EMERGENCY/DOCK_STATUS subkinds, NODE_LANTERN, DEPLOYABLE/GLOWSTICK, BEACON, FAULT_GLOW); a seventh kind is a schema bump; no record has phantom/perceived/decoy/hallucinated fields. | Data | EM-3, EM-29 |
| TR-emitter-007 | Canonical (snapshotted, hashed) state is limited to the id counter, canonical record fields (incl. switch_on, arm_tick, last_toggle_tick, life/evict ticks, FAULT_GLOW placed_tick/glow_key/sev) and subject registrations including each subject's `lit` hysteresis bit; body_id, origin/aim/reach/output_pm, pair rows, lux values and read-view snapshots are derived and never hashed. | Save/Load | EM-4, EM-22, EM-28 |
| TR-emitter-008 | `post_restore` rebuilds all derived state in ascending id (including the whole static layer, so no subject is pending at the first validate), keeps the subject `lit` bit, re-derives body_id from Layout/Body, and a snapshot restored at any tick yields identical answers from T+1 on (kernel G4 save-equivalence). | Save/Load | EM-28, AC-41, AC-54 |
| TR-emitter-009 | The kernel binding source `beam_bindings() -> [(player_id, beam_id)]` (ascending player_id, pure read) is registered at BOOTING so the LOADING rebuild binds seat beams after every post_restore; `toggle_beam` uses actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER with actor_source `emitter.state`. | Core | EM-7, EM-28, E9 |
| TR-emitter-010 | `toggle_beam` (origin PLAYER, coalesce NONE, max_age_ticks 120) validates in order NO_SUCH_EMITTER, NOT_ACTIONABLE, TOO_SOON, CHARGE_EMPTY; the beam changes only on committed state and the Presenter never predicts it. | Input | EM-7 |
| TR-emitter-011 | A sim-side commit-spacing guard rejects `toggle_beam` (TOO_SOON) and `set_switch` (COOLDOWN, all origins) when a realised transition is within SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS (12) of canonical `last_toggle_tick`; an OFF during ARMING is exempt; E10 is exempt. | Core | EM-7, D.2b |
| TR-emitter-012 | `set_switch` (PLAYER toggle / SYSTEM {emitter_id,on}) and `set_beacon` (SYSTEM only) validate against 'structurally present' only (NOT_LIVE, NOT_SWITCHABLE, NOT_BEACON, NO_SUCH_EMITTER); PLAYER-origin validate never reads node state, served_pm or health (no oracle). | Core | EM-7, EM-13 |
| TR-emitter-013 | Fixture ON calls Graph M14 `set_load_request(node_ref, req_w)` inside the apply, the lamp is ARMING (output 0) until arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS) (0..5 ticks), and OFF is immediate with M14 (node_ref, 0). | Threading/Timing | EM-12, D.2 |
